summary: Qwen3.8-27B is Alibaba's 27B dense, natively multimodal (text/image/video) open-weight model, released 2026-08-14 under Apache 2.0, with a 262,144-token native context (extensible to 1M via YaRN). '52' is real but has a shelf life: it was the model's *then-current* Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score under index version v4.1.1 (snapshot 2026-08-18, 'Intelligence #1 / 135'; HN thread 'Qwen3.8 27B scores 52 on Artificial Analysis', 381 points, 180 comments). Artificial Analysis has since re-versioned the index twice (v4.2 removed GPQA Diamond; v4.3 replaced tau3-Banking with AutomationBench-AA and upgraded Terminal-Bench 2.1 -> 4.0; current build v4.3.2, announced 'Update Intelligence Index v4.3'). As of 2026-10-01 the same live URL states 'Qwen3.8 27B (Xhigh) scores 34 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index' (#1 / 142, 4 of 4 units for Intelligence, median 8 for open-weight models of similar size). So the honest answer to 'is it 52?' is: yes, that was the score at launch and in every August article; no, it is 34 on today's index, and the gap is re-baselining, not a regression. The interesting story is not the absolute number but the shape of the profile, which has NOT changed: a 27B dense model that beats much larger models on agentic/tool-use/computer-use work while trailing them on knowledge-heavy reasoning, at the cost of extreme verbosity and slow generation.

competitors.title: Artificial Analysis - Qwen3.8 27B (xhigh) model page (PRIMARY, live as of 2026-10-01)
key_points: PRIMARY SOURCE, current state: 'Qwen3.8 27B (Xhigh) scores 34 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, placing it well above average among comparable models (median: 8)'.

Rank card reads '# 1 / 142' for Intelligence with '4 out of 4 units for Intelligence'; Speed '# 54 / 142' at 45.1 tok/s ('notably slow', '1 out of 4 units for Speed'); Cost '# 18 / 142', $1.01 cost per Intelligence Index task ('4 out of 4 units for Cost'); Verbosity '# 22 / 142' at 200M output tokens ('4 out of 4 units for Verbosity').

IMPORTANT RANK CAVEAT: the '# 1 / 142' badge is the model page's default comparison group. AA's stated comparison rule is that open-weights models are compared only with other open-weights models of the same size class (Tiny <=4B, Small 4B-40B, Medium 40B-150B, Large >150B), so 27B sits in 'Small'; the 'median: 8' figure is the comparable-cohort median. Do not present '# 1 / 142' as a global #1.
Verbatim verdict text: 'amongst the leading models in intelligence, but particularly expensive when comparing to other open weight models of similar size. It's also notably slow and very verbose.'

Serving economics on AA's page: $0.50 / 1M input, $3.00 / 1M output, 80% cache discount, average $1.01 per Intelligence Index task; 45 tok/s; time to first answer token 48.23s; end-to-end response time 59.31s; time per task 1233.15s.

AA's index version note on the page: 'Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2 incorporates 10 evaluations: AA-Briefcase v1.1, GDPval-AA v2.1, AutomationBench-AA, Terminal-Bench 4.0, SciCode, Humanity's Last Exam, GDP.pdf, CritPt, AA-Omniscience, AA-LCR v1.1'.

Per-benchmark (v4.3.2, from the comparison view): AA-Briefcase v1.1 1401, GDPval-AA v2.1 1411, AutomationBench-AA 48%, Terminal-Bench 4.0 6%, SciCode 47%, Humanity's Last Exam 34%, GDP.pdf 17%, CritPt 5%, AA-Omniscience -10, AA-LCR v1.1 82%.

Technical summary on page: 27B total parameters, 40B 'active parameters' figure listed in the comparison table, reasoning = Yes, context 256k, input text/image/video, output text, Apache 2.0, released August 2026.

competitors.title: Wayback snapshot 2026-08-18 of the same AA page (PROOF of the 52)
key_points: PROOF THE '52' WAS REAL: archived 2026-08-18T23:59:16Z, page read 'Qwen3.8 27B scores 52 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index', 'Intelligence # 1 / 135', '52 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index', verbosity '# 23 / 135', '160M Output tokens from Intelligence Index'.

Snapshot's index banner: 'Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.1.1 incorporates 9 evaluations: GDPval-AA v2, tau3-Banking, Terminal-Bench v2.1, SciCode, Humanity's Last Exam, GPQA Diamond, CritPt, AA-Omniscience, AA-LCR' with '29 of 610 models' in the comparison pool.

At that time cost was reported as In $0.00 / Out $0.00 with Speed N/A, i.e. no first-party hosted endpoint yet; today's page prices the model at $0.50/$3.00 and reports 45.1 tok/s from Alibaba's API. Pricing/speed were added, not changed.
Direct comparison of the two snapshots gives the article its centrepiece: same model, same xhigh reasoning, 52 -> 34 purely from index version v4.1.1 -> v4.3.2.

competitors.title: AA Intelligence Benchmarking Methodology (index version history)
key_points: Current version: 'Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2 incorporates 10 evaluations: AA-Briefcase v1.1, GDPval-AA v2.1, AutomationBench-AA, Terminal-Bench 4.0, SciCode, AA-LCR v1.1, AA-Omniscience, Humanity's Last Exam, GDP.pdf, CritPt.'

competitors.title: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B official model card (vendor self-reported benchmarks)
key_points: Architecture detail a comparison article needs: 27B params, hidden dim 5120, 64 layers, layout '16 x (3 x (Gated DeltaNet -> FFN) -> 1 x (Gated Attention -> FFN))' - a 3:1 hybrid of linear attention (Gated DeltaNet: 48 V heads, 16 QK heads, head dim 128) to full gated attention (24 Q heads, 4 KV heads, head dim 256, RoPE dim 64); FFN intermediate 17,408; vocab 248,320; MTP trained with multiple steps.
Context: '262,144 natively and extensible up to 1,000,000 tokens.'

Text benchmarks (vendor): Terminal Bench 2.1 73.0, SWE-bench Pro 61.7, NL2Repo-Bench 42.3, DeepSWE 1.1 42.2, QwenSWEBench 79.0, CoWorkBench 70.7, JobBench 33.4, Agents' Last Exam 20.4 Pass@1 / 42.9 score, IFBench 79.5, GPQA Diamond 89.2, HLE 30.8, LiveCodeBench v6 90.3.

Vision/agentic benchmarks (vendor): OSWorld-Verified 84.3, WebArena-Verified 64.8, AndroidWorld 81.9, RecreationBench 47.1, ClawEval-MM 57.4 Pass@3, SWE-MM 38.6, Vision2Web 62.9; MathVision 90.0 (94.6 w/ CI), BabyVision 65.7 (85.6 w/ CI), CharXiv RQ 83.7 (90.2 w/ CI), OmniDocBench 1.5 91.1, RealWorldQA 85.9, ERQA 65.5.
These tables also carry the comparison columns Qwen3.6-27B, Qwen3.7-Plus (closed weight), Muse Glimmer-30B and Opus 4.6 Max - the cleanest source for the 'beats Opus on X, loses on Y' argument.

Thinking control: 'Thinking mode is on by default and can be disabled per request; reasoning depth can be tuned with reasoning_effort, and reasoning context from historical messages is retained via preserve_thinking.'
Card also points at a hosted Qwen Cloud version promised with '1M context length by default, official built-in tools' listed as 'coming soon'.

competitors.title: AlibabaCloud-Official/Qwen3.8-27B repo (via gh api, 2026-10-01)
key_points: Created 2026-08-14T15:22:15Z, last pushed 2026-08-14T15:38:21Z (21 minutes of activity), Apache-2.0, 45 stars, 1 fork, no releases or tags - a model-card repo, not an engineering project. Useful as a release-date proof point.

Repo description: 'Native multimodal dense LLM with 27B params outperforming Qwen3.7-Plus in coding & office workflows. Features 262K native context, extendable to 1M via YaRN. Licensed under Apache 2.0.'
README lists official access paths: Hugging Face collection (huggingface.co/collections/Qwen/qwen38), ModelScope, Unsloth GGUF, Qwen Cloud, Alibaba Cloud Model Studio.

competitors.title: Simon Willison - 'Qwen 3.8 27B is excellent, but it defaults to wildly overthinking things' (2026-08-16)
key_points: The best independent counterweight to the benchmark number, published 2 days after launch: the xhigh default 'results in spectacular over-thinking'. His pelican-on-a-bicycle SVG 'took 21 minutes to generate, using 22,276 reasoning tokens to produce 3,223 tokens of output'; with reasoning off the same prompt produced 3,715 tokens in 137s.

He documents the actual reasoning_effort ladder from Qwen's docs: 'xhigh (default): for complex tasks demanding thorough analysis / medium: balancing accuracy and speed / low: efficient reasoning optimizing for speed and cost', and calls the default 'hilarious... absolutely not a good way to run the model, especially on consumer hardware'.

Hardware reality check: ran the 17GB Q4_K_M quant via LM Studio on a 128GB M5 Max MacBook Pro and an NVIDIA DGX Spark; hit LM Studio's 8,192-token default context limit because the model spent it all 'thinking about even the most mundane of problems'; had to load the full 262,144 context.
Also useful for the 'benchmark moment' framing: Qwen 3.8 27B vs open-weight Qwen 3.8 2.4T-A95B on the same prompt (the 2.4T produced an animated SVG).

competitors.title: Hacker News discussion - 'Qwen3.8 27B scores 52 on Artificial Analysis' (2026-08-17)
key_points: The headline's origin: submitted 2026-08-17T17:25:17Z directly linking the AA model page, 381 points, 180 comments, 34 top-level threads - the single best source of 'what practitioners argued about', and the article should quote it rather than paraphrase benchmark tables.
Score-context arguments: 'Qwen3.6 27B scores 38... Qwen3.8 27B beats all medium models (40B-150B). It has the same score as DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731, which ranks #5 in large model category (>150B).'

Skepticism thread (essential for balance): 'This one is very benchmaxxed, and you can tell from this page alone. Look at the huge variance in ranking per benchmark'; 'A lot of the benchmarks seem often near meaningless these days - really bench-maxxed to the hilt'; counterpoint from a practitioner: 'Qwen 3.8 27B doesn't look benchmaxxed... These "52 AA score" numbers feel real, which is surprising' (internal automated benchmark).

Verbosity/token economics debate: comments that the model produces ~2x the tokens per task of its predecessor and ~2.3x GPT-5.6 Luna, hurting local deployment; another calls out 45 tok/s vs DeepSeek V4 Flash at a fraction of the RAM.
Best structural quote for the cost argument: 'It's 27b active params vs 13b active params, so you'd expect it to be ~2x more expensive when serving multiple users.'

Practitioner field reports on agentic behaviour: 'It gets really agentic at the higher reasoning levels... it gets obsessed with solving problems and will do insane/unusual things to get to the solution', plus a complaint that it would not stop a multi-hour turn to answer questions.

Hallucination-rate praise: 'I want to highlight its (1-hallucation rate) at 70%. BRAVO! For me, this is its most wonderful score. GPT-5.6-Sol sits at 8%.' (commenter's own correction: 'non-hallucination rate').
Ranking-position claims worth re-verifying before publishing: 'It's 7th (!!!) overall on the agentic index, above Terra', 'Strangely Qwen 3.8 Max isn't on their list, at all'.

competitors.title: Qubrid - 'Qwen3.8-27B Benchmarks: Official and Independent Results' (updated 2026-08-31)
key_points: Best single secondary source on methodology hygiene, and it explicitly labels vendor vs independent numbers: 'Qwen3.8-27B scores 52 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at maximum reasoning effort and 61.7 on SWE-bench Pro per Qwen's own evaluation.'

It separates 'official benchmarks' (model card) from 'independent benchmarks: Artificial Analysis', and has dedicated sections for 'The Agentic Index, and a number that gets misquoted constantly' and 'Methodology caveats you should actually read' - a good structural model to adapt.

Caveat content to reuse: 'Qwen3.8-27B outperforms Claude Opus 4.6 Max on 16 of the 24 benchmarks in its official model card', but 'VentureBeat also points out that some evaluations are internal and the harnesses are not identical across every comparison, which makes the numbers poor grounds for declaring a universal winner.'
Its reading of the profile matches the primary data: 'this model converts its parameter budget into agentic and tool-use performance unusually well, and into broad frontier knowledge less well.'

competitors.title: Regolo AI - 'every test where Alibaba's 27B model beats Claude Opus 4.6 Max' (2026-08-21)
key_points: Sharpest framing of the vendor table, with explicit naming of the wins and losses: 'outperforms Claude Opus 4.6 Max on 16 of the 24 benchmarks', biggest wins SWE-bench Pro (61.7 vs 53.4), IFBench (79.5 vs 62.5), OSWorld-Verified (84.3 vs 72.7); still loses Humanity's Last Exam (30.8 vs 40.0).
States the provenance caveat plainly: 'Every number is self-reported by Alibaba; no independent reproduction existed at launch. Treat the table as a ceiling, not a floor.'
Notes it wins every overlapping row against Muse Glimmer-30B, the other open-weight comparator in the card.
Also a good example of a competitor page that mixes real analysis with a hosted-API upsell (EU/sovereign hosting, 262K context claim) - useful for spotting where SEO competitors pivot to sales copy.

competitors.title: Codersera - 'Qwen3.8-27B Complete Guide: Benchmarks, VRAM, vs Claude' (2026-08-18)
key_points: Direct keyword competitor for the primary term, and the cleanest example of the claim this article must correct: 'It scores 52 on Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index - up 14 points over Qwen3.6-27B on an identical architecture', published 2026-08-18 and last updated 2026-08-18 (i.e. never re-checked after the index re-versioned).
Confirms the 17-18GB footprint framing: 'fits in an 18 GB Ollama download, and is currently the strongest local coding agent you can run'.

Release-timeline framing worth reusing (verify before publishing): three Qwen releases in twelve days in August 2026 - Qwen3.8-Max GA on the 3rd, the 2.4T open flagship on the 12th, Qwen3.8-27B on the 14th.
Structure (Quick answer -> benchmarks -> VRAM -> vs Claude) is close to what a searcher for 'Qwen3.8 27B benchmark' wants; differentiate with the index-version analysis and primary AA data.

competitors.title: Hoja - 'Qwen3.8-27B: the same architecture, fourteen points better' (2026-08-24)
key_points: The best statement of the most under-explained fact: 'scores 52 on the Artificial Analysis index against its predecessor's 38, with an identical network' - the gain is post-training, not architecture. Section title says it: 'The upgrade is entirely post-training'.

Details the inherited base: 'The network is the same one it shipped in April: 27 billion dense parameters, 64 layers, the same hybrid of Gated DeltaNet and gated attention, the same 262,144-token context, the same vision encoder.'

Has a section literally titled 'What fourteen points do not prove' plus 'Where it actually sits against the frontier' and 'It costs to run it in memory, honestly' - useful competitor structure to outperform.
Written from the local-inference/hardware angle ('running a capable model on one graphics card, and what it costs in memory and tokens').

competitors.title: Quesma - 'Benchmarking Qwen3.8 27B quantizations: 4-bit holds up, 1-bit collapses' (2026-08-26, HN front page 2026-09-08)
key_points: Independent quantization study by Piotr Migdal: 'The full BF16 model weighs 55 GB... Yet the 17 GB Q4_K_M matches the full model on a popular agentic coding benchmark, Terminal-Bench 2.1. It fits on a 24 GB card such as RTX 4090, still leaving room for about 64k tokens of context.'
The cliff: 'At 1 bit, the model performs around random chance on GPQA Diamond, and longer reasoning makes it worse.'
Quant ladder actually tested: Q8_0 (29 GB), Q4_K_M (17 GB), UD-Q2_K_XL (10.7 GB), UD-IQ1_S (6.2 GB). Useful concrete numbers for a VRAM section.
Second HN front page for the model (286 points, 139 comments) a month after launch - evidence that local-deployment interest outlived the launch spike.

competitors.title: TerminalBytes - 'Run Qwen3.8 27B locally: real numbers from my Mac Studio' (2026-08-27)
key_points: Measured local throughput on an M3 Ultra Mac Studio: 'Qwen3.8 27B (Q4_K_M, 17GB) generates at ~14 tokens/s... Its predecessor qwen3.6:27b does ~28.6 tokens/s on the same machine' - i.e. roughly half the speed of the previous generation for the same prompt set.
Five timed runs per model, same prompts, same machine; includes a '1-bit experiment: brain damage, measured' section.
Usage framing that matches the AA verbosity finding: a background assistant for RSS digests and filing scanned PDFs rather than interactive use.
Independent corroboration (140 points, 99 comments on HN 2026-08-28) that the verbosity/speed tradeoff is the real-world complaint.

competitors.title: Michal Piszczek - 'Qwen3.8 27B at 256K: 50 TPS on a 24 GB GPU' (2026-08-17, updated 08-18)
key_points: The most rigorous local-serving writeup found (HackerNoon editor pick 2026-08-19, 17 min read, 38 points/36 comments on HN): targets 256K context on a 24GB GPU and reports ~50 tok/s, which contradicts the naive 'xhigh is always unusable' framing in a useful way.

Documents failure modes rather than just a win: 'The first winner was Q4_0, and it was the wrong winner', 'The ready-made NVFP4 quant failed the quality gate', 'MTP had a trapdoor at n=8', 'More accurate MTP made the system worse'.
Good source for the argument that Qwen3.8 27B's practical viability depends heavily on quant choice, MTP/speculative decoding configuration and context budget - not on the headline benchmark number.

competitors.title: Unsloth GGUF quantizations (exact file sizes)
key_points: Authoritative size table for a VRAM section, in GB on disk: UD-IQ1_S 6.19, UD-IQ1_M 6.73, UD-IQ2_XXS 7.27, UD-IQ2_S 8.37, UD-Q2_K_XL 9.83, UD-IQ3_XXS 10.9, UD-IQ3_S 12, UD-Q3_K_XL 13.1, UD-IQ4_XS 14.3, UD-Q4_K_S 15.4, Q4_0 16.1, UD-Q4_K_M 16.5, Q4_1 17.5, UD-Q4_K_XL 17.6, UD-Q5_K_S 18.7, UD-Q5_K_M 19.8, UD-Q5_K_XL 20.9, UD-Q6_K 22, UD-Q6_K_M 23.1, UD-Q6_K_L 24.2, UD-Q6_K_XL 25.3, Q8_0 29, UD-Q8_K_XL 31.5, BF16 54.7.

Documented one-liners for the how-to angle: 'llama serve -hf unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_M' and 'winget install llama.cpp'.

competitors.title: Qwen Cloud hosted model page (first-party serving features)
key_points: First-party hosted feature set for the 'if you don't want to self-host' half of a comparison: prefix completion (partial mode), function calling, context cache, structured outputs, batch, input text/image/video, output text.
Frames the hosted model as building on 3.6-27B 'with key improvements in coding and office productivity capabilities across both text and visual modalities'.

Note: the /pricing sub-page returned 404 on 2026-10-01, so use AA's price card ($0.50 in / $3.00 out, 80% cache discount) as the pricing source and mention list price provenance rather than guessing Qwen Cloud rates.

Related first-party artifact worth a follow-up check before publishing: an official 'Qwen3.8-27B-FP8' weights repo exists (huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8) and NVIDIA NGC lists a Qwen3.8-27B NIM container.

competitors.title: dev.to - 'Qwen 3.8 27B: The Frontier LLM That Fits on Your Laptop' (2026-09-16)
key_points: Most recent competitor article found (republished 2026-09-16, ~18 min read) and it still repeats the August claim: 'The Benchmark Moment Nobody Saw Coming... on August 15-16, 2026, Alibaba's Qwen team dropped a 17-gigabyte file on Hugging Face' (Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf).
Deep-dive structure worth mining for the architecture section: Gated DeltaNet hybrid attention, and Multi-Token Prediction 'as a built-in speculative decoder'.
Covers the reasoning_effort API paradigm and agentic integration (harness support) - the two most practical sections for developers.
Its weakness is exactly the freshness gap this article exploits: it sells the launch moment without re-checking AA after the index moved to v4.3.

competitors.title: AA leaderboard home (index version banner + agentic index)
key_points: Live banner on 2026-10-01: 'Update Intelligence Index v4.3. Intelligence Index v4.3 replaces tau3-Banking with AutomationBench-AA, and upgrades Terminal-Bench to 4.0' plus 'New Announcing the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index'.
This is the page to cite for 'the index itself changed after launch', and the landing page for re-checking the agentic-index claims made in the HN thread.

The agentic chart on this page renders client-side; the leaderboard position numbers could not be read from static HTML, so any '7th overall on the agentic index' claim in the article must be re-verified in a browser before publishing.

stats.fact: Qwen3.8 27B was released 2026-08-14 under Apache 2.0, created at 2026-08-14T15:22:15Z on GitHub with the last push 21 minutes later at 15:38:21Z.

'52' is the correct Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score as of 2026-08-18, under index version v4.1.1 ('# 1 / 135', median 9 for the comparable cohort) - verified in the Wayback snapshot of the model page.

As of 2026-10-01 the same live URL reports 34, not 52: 'Qwen3.8 27B (Xhigh) scores 34 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, placing it well above average among comparable models (median: 8)' - the change comes from index re-versioning, not model re-testing.

The index moved from v4.1.1 (9 evaluations, incl. GPQA Diamond and tau3-Banking) to v4.3.2 (10 evaluations: AA-Briefcase v1.1, GDPval-AA v2.1, AutomationBench-AA, Terminal-Bench 4.0, SciCode, HLE, GDP.pdf, CritPt, AA-Omniscience, AA-LCR v1.1). GPQA Diamond was removed in v4.2, tau3-Banking in v4.3, Terminal-Bench 2.1 superseded by 4.0 in v4.3.

Current per-benchmark scores (v4.3.2) for Qwen3.8 27B vs GLM-5.2: AA-Briefcase 1401 vs 1230; GDPval-AA 1411 vs 1358; AutomationBench-AA 48% vs 28%; Terminal-Bench 4.0 6% vs 1%; SciCode 47% vs 51%; HLE 34% vs 41%; GDP.pdf 17% vs 10%; CritPt 5% vs 21%; AA-Omniscience -10 vs 4; AA-LCR 82% vs 78%.

AA currently ranks it '# 1 / 142' on Intelligence with 4/4 units, but also '# 54 / 142' on speed (45.1 tok/s, 1/4 units), '# 18 / 142' on cost and '# 22 / 142' on verbosity (200M output tokens) - and AA's own rule is that open-weight models are compared only against open-weight models of the same size class (Small = 4B-40B).

AA verdict on the model today: 'amongst the leading models in intelligence, but particularly expensive when comparing to other open weight models of similar size. It's also notably slow and very verbose.'

In the August v4.1.1 snapshot the AA page reported 160M output tokens for the index and '# 23 / 135' on verbosity; today it reports 200M tokens and '# 22 / 142' - token accounting itself changed with the index version, while the verbosity verdict did not.

Serving economics (AA, 2026-10-01): $0.50 per 1M input tokens, $3.00 per 1M output tokens, 80% cache discount, $0.10 cache-hit price, average $1.01 per Intelligence Index task, 45 tok/s, 48.23s time to first answer token, 1233.15s per task.

The HN launch thread 'Qwen3.8 27B scores 52 on Artificial Analysis' (submitted 2026-08-17T17:25:17Z, linking the AA page) reached 381 points and 180 comments - the highest-engagement item about this model.

A second front-page HN thread a month later - 'Benchmarking Qwen3.8 27B quantizations: 4-bit holds up, 1-bit collapses' (2026-09-08) - drew 286 points and 139 comments, showing durable local-deployment interest.

Vendor-reported agentic gains over the previous generation: DeepSWE 1.1 rose 13.3 -> 42.2 and QwenSWEBench 49.3 -> 79.0 between Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3.8-27B; SWE-bench Pro 61.7 and Terminal Bench 2.1 73.0.

Against Claude Opus 4.6 Max (all vendor-reported, harnesses not identical): wins SWE-bench Pro 61.7 vs 53.4, IFBench 79.5 vs 62.5, OSWorld-Verified 84.3 vs 72.7, AndroidWorld 81.9 vs 62.0, LiveCodeBench v6 90.3 vs 88.8; loses HLE 30.8 vs 40.0, GPQA Diamond 89.2 vs 91.3, Agents' Last Exam, OmniDocBench 91.1 vs 86.6 is a win (verify per row before quoting).

The architecture is unchanged from Qwen3.6-27B - same 27B dense network, 64 layers, same Gated DeltaNet/gated attention hybrid, same 262,144-token context, same vision encoder - so the benchmark jump is entirely post-training.

Official architecture spec: 27B params, hidden dim 5120, 64 layers, hidden layout 16 x (3 x (Gated DeltaNet -> FFN) -> 1 x (Gated Attention -> FFN)), Gated DeltaNet 48 V-heads/16 QK-heads at head dim 128, gated attention 24 Q-heads/4 KV-heads at head dim 256, FFN intermediate 17,408, vocab 248,320, MTP trained with multiple steps.

Q4_K_M (17 GB) matches the full BF16 model on Terminal-Bench 2.1 while fitting a 24 GB card with roughly 64k tokens of context left over; at 1-bit the model performs around random chance on GPQA Diamond and longer reasoning makes it worse.

GGUF sizes on disk from Unsloth: 1-bit UD-IQ1_S 6.19 GB; 2-bit UD-Q2_K_XL 9.83 GB; 4-bit UD-Q4_K_M 16.5 GB; 8-bit Q8_0 29 GB; BF16 54.7 GB - plus a separate 1.37 GB MTP Q4_0 speculative-decoding head.
Local throughput measured on an M3 Ultra Mac Studio: ~14 tok/s for Qwen3.8 27B (Q4_K_M, 17GB) versus ~28.6 tok/s for qwen3.6:27b on the same machine and prompts.

With the default xhigh reasoning effort, a single pelican-on-a-bicycle SVG took 21 minutes and 22,276 reasoning tokens to produce 3,223 output tokens; with reasoning off the same prompt took 137s and 3,715 tokens. Qwen's documented ladder is xhigh (default, 'complex tasks demanding thorough analysis') / medium / low.

AA states the Intelligence Index is 'a primarily text-based, English-language evaluation' and targets <+/-1% error on the index overall while warning that individual evaluations have wider confidence intervals - so a 1-2 point gap between neighbouring models is not a real difference.

Practitioner skepticism on '52' as a quality proxy (HN): 'This one is very benchmaxxed, and you can tell from this page alone. Look at the huge variance in ranking per benchmark' - answered by an independent tester: 'Qwen 3.8 27B doesn't look benchmaxxed... These "52 AA score" numbers feel real.'

Token-cost shape versus larger peers (HN): the model is reported to use ~2x the tokens per task of Qwen3.6 27B and ~2.3x GPT-5.6 Luna, and a commenter frames the serving cost as structural: 'It's 27b active params vs 13b active params, so you'd expect it to be ~2x more expensive when serving multiple users.'
At launch there was no first-party hosted endpoint (AA showed In $0.00 / Out $0.00 and Speed N/A); by 2026-10-01 AA prices it from Alibaba's API at $0.50/$3.00 with 45.1 tok/s.
stats.source: Wayback 2026-08-18 snapshot vs live AA page 2026-10-01

angles: 'The 52 is real, and it is already out of date': the index re-versioned twice after launch (v4.1.1 -> v4.2 -> v4.3.2, GPQA Diamond and tau3-Banking removed, Terminal-Bench 2.1 -> 4.0), so the same model now scores 34. Every competitor article checked still quotes 52 with an August date and none re-verified it - that is the freshness wedge for this post.

Explain WHY the number moved instead of just reporting the new one: what GPQA Diamond and tau3-Banking were worth to this model, what AutomationBench-AA and Terminal-Bench 4.0 measure, and why a 27B agentic model loses points when the index swaps knowledge benchmarks for agentic ones. Include AA's own <+/-1% precision note to kill false precision.

The profile is the story, not the total: this model wins on agentic/tool-use/computer-use rows (AutomationBench-AA 48% vs GLM-5.2's 28%, OSWorld-Verified 84.3, AndroidWorld 81.9) and loses on knowledge rows (HLE 34% vs 41%, AA-Omniscience -10 vs 4, CritPt 5% vs 21%). 'Beats Opus at doing, loses to Opus at knowing' is the memorable one-liner, with the caveat that those rows are vendor-reported.

Identical network, +14 points: the whole generational jump came from post-training, not architecture. Use the official layout spec (3:1 Gated DeltaNet to gated attention hybrid, MTP head) to show what was already there and what changed.

The hidden tax: verbosity. AA reports 200M output tokens for the index against an 82M median and grades it 1/4 on speed at 45.1 tok/s; on an M3 Ultra the model runs ~14 tok/s, about half its own predecessor. Pair with Simon Willison's 21-minute pelican and 22,276 reasoning tokens and the 'reasoning_effort xhigh is a terrible default' argument - then give the fix (low/medium, or disable thinking).

Cost paradox: a model you can download for free costs $1.01 per Intelligence Index task on a hosted endpoint and is described by AA as 'particularly expensive' versus open-weight peers of similar size, because it is dense (27B active) and verbose - not because it is large.

Deployment reality check as a service to the reader: 4-bit holds up (Q4_K_M 17GB matches BF16 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, fits a 24GB card with ~64k context), 1-bit collapses (random chance on GPQA Diamond), and quant/MTP/context choices matter more in practice than the index score. Include the exact Unsloth size table.

The benchmaxxing debate, handled fairly: quote both the 'very benchmaxxed, look at the variance per benchmark' critique and the independent practitioner who tested it against an internal workflow and said the 52 'feels real'. End with what a reader should measure for themselves.

Position in the August 2026 Qwen blitz: Qwen3.8-Max (Aug 3), Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B (Aug 12), Qwen3.8-27B (Aug 14) - the 27B is the one that runs on hardware you own. Note the 2.4T sibling as the ceiling for the same family (Willison's animated SVG comparison).

One month of evidence after the launch spike: quantization study on HN front page (2026-09-08, 286 points), a 'real numbers from my Mac Studio' writeup (2026-08-28, 140 points), and a 256K-on-24GB-GPU engineering report - enough track record to write about the model as a durable local worker rather than a launch-day wonder.

notes_for_writer: LEAD WITH THE CORRECTION, NOT WITH 52: the single most valuable thing this article can do is state that 52 was the score under index v4.1.1 on 2026-08-18 and that the same AA page now says 34 under v4.3.2. Every competitor article checked still prints 52 without a re-check.

NEVER present 52 and 34 as a quality regression. They are different index versions with different constituent benchmarks (GPQA Diamond removed in v4.2, tau3-Banking removed and Terminal-Bench 2.1 -> 4.0 in v4.3).

Label provenance on every number: 'Alibaba reports' / 'Qwen's model card says' for vendor tables, 'Artificial Analysis measured' for AA figures. The 61.7 SWE-bench Pro and 89.2 GPQA Diamond are VENDOR numbers and were not independently reproduced at launch.

Do not call '# 1 / 142' a global ranking: AA compares open-weight models only against other open-weight models in the same size class (Small = 4B-40B). Say '#1 among open-weight small models in AA's default view'.

The model is 'xhigh' by default and the article should say so wherever generation speed or quality is discussed - xhigh is the configuration AA measures, and it is also the configuration Simon Willison calls 'absolutely not a good way to run the model'.

Use concrete local numbers (14 tok/s on M3 Ultra at Q4_K_M; ~50 tok/s at 256K on a 24GB GPU with the right quant/MTP setup; 6.19 GB to 54.7 GB quant range) rather than vague 'runs on consumer hardware' claims.
Include the benchmaxxing counter-argument and the practitioner rebuttal in the same section - the HN thread is the best source and the topic is polarising, which is good for engagement and for trust.

Verify before publishing: the AA agentic-index rank (~7th) claim, Qwen Cloud pricing, the exact Qwen3.8-Max/2.4T release dates, and whether the hosted 1M-context Qwen Cloud endpoint has actually launched (the HF card said 'coming soon' as of the model card revision).
